items.why: Notetaker moved inside the HIPAA/BAA compliance scope (only Scratchpad still excluded); no price, plan or limit changed.
Qwen3.7-Max serverless inference rose 67% (input $1.50 → $2.50, cached $0.30 → $0.50, output $4.50 → $7.50 per 1M tokens) and four models left the serverless lineup.

record.short: Qwen3.7-Max serverless inference rises from $1.50 to $2.50 input and from $4.50 to $7.50 output per 1M tokens.
record.headline: Together AI raised Qwen3.7-Max serverless inference prices by 67% on input, cached input and output, and removed four models from its serverless list.
record.who: Anyone calling Qwen3.7-Max through Together serverless inference; users of the four removed models must migrate.
record.read: A per-token rate that has moved several times since September makes margins on inference-based features hard to hold. The model removals add a forced-migration cost for some teams.
record.caveat: The structured field on the PricingSaaS page reads $4.50 → $2.50 (−44%), which contradicts its own text; we follow the text, which gives input, cached and output rates and a 67% rise. The removed models are Inkling, Cogito v2.1 671B, Llama 3 8B Instruct Lite and Qwen3 235B A22B Instruct 2507 FP8 Throughput.

items.why: Syren video limit changed from a flat 'Up to 3 minutes' per generation to per-plan monthly video counts (1 Basic, ~2 Starter, ~7 Pro).

record.short: Syren is now capped by monthly video count (1 on Basic, about 2 on Starter, about 7 on Pro) instead of up to 3 minutes per generation.
record.headline: Synthesia replaced the flat 3-minute cap on each Syren generation with a monthly video-count quota that differs by plan, and relabelled the row from Video length to Video generation.
record.who: Customers on Basic, Starter and Pro using the Syren AI video agent.
record.read: Capping by count rather than length is easier to budget but gives short clips no advantage. Syren launched only weeks ago, so the metric is still being settled.
record.caveat: PricingSaaS reports a live A/B test on Synthesia's plan cards, and the quotas shown now match one arm of it, so this may not be final.

items.why: Nano Banana 2 image cost fell from 8 to 7 credits, so top-up packs yield more images at unchanged prices (a separate change from the earlier plan credit cut).

record.short: Nano Banana 2 now costs 7 credits per image instead of 8, so the $25 top-up pack yields 214 images instead of 187 at an unchanged price.

items.why: The per-tier Custom AI Meeting Templates usage row was removed from the comparison table; nothing shows the limits themselves changed, only that they are no longer listed.
Claude Haiku 5.5 added to the rate card at $0.10 input / $0.50 output per 1M tokens; Haiku 4.5 and other prices unchanged.
Video-to-Video is now billed per second of generated plus reference video with displayed rates halved; Flux 3 video rates cut, MiniMax H3 Max V2V raised, Kling 4.0 Flash models added.

record.short: Video-to-Video is now billed per second of generated plus reference video, with Seedance 2.0 720p shown at 32 credits/sec instead of 64, while Flux 3 HD video falls from 60 to 50 and MiniMax H3 Max 768p V2V rises from 73 to 82.

items.why: Nano Banana 2.1 (1K) now costs about 25 units per image instead of 22, cutting per-plan image estimates about 11% at unchanged prices.

record.short: Nano Banana 2.1 now costs about 25 units per image instead of 22, so plan estimates fall about 11% (Basic 225 → 200, Pro 900 → 803) at unchanged prices.
